extracted.intended_audience: general readers and fans of comedy podcasts; people researching podcast formats or the show '2 Dope Queens'
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the production and format features of the comedy podcast 2 Dope Queens, including episode length, recording setup, guest structure, topical scope, and representation goals. Useful for understanding how this specific show was produced and presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode running time / editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the live show runs about two hours, the podcast is edited down to about an hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied production standard: record longer live performances and edit them to a roughly one-hour podcast episode for release; editing decisions determine final runtime and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording format / live taping
rubrics_metrics.description: 2 Dope Queens is taped live at Union Hall in Brooklyn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied production characteristic: record in front of a live audience (club/venue), which shapes performance energy, audience interaction, and potential editing needs (crowd noise, timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode structure / guest count
rubrics_metrics.description: Each episode features three guest comedians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a structural norm: plan episodes around three performers/guests, which informs segment length, pacing, and show flow when editing down from the live show to the podcast runtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical scope / themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues discussed on the podcast include "race, gender, sex, and other topics".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content guideline: center conversations and stand-up around social identity and interpersonal topics; producers may prioritize episodes that address these themes to maintain show identity and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation / casting priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The podcast features female comedians, comedians of color, and LGBT comedians, in an effort to represent people from different backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/booking standard: actively seek and showcase performers from underrepresented groups to increase diversity of voices and perspectives; aligns with the hosts' stated mission to let marginalized performers be central rather than supporting characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host approach / spotlighting guests' stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Host Jessica Williams said: "For our show, people get to be the stars of their own stories and they get to be the stars of their own stand up... give our friends and a lot of people of color and different orientations an opportunity to speak for themselves and be sort of the main character as opposed to like the side character or supporting character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylistic guideline: the hosts emphasize enabling performers to tell personal stories and perform stand-up that centers their perspectives; production and hosting choices should support and foreground guest narratives rather than host-centric formats.
